I'd installed a smart lock a few months back, mostly so I could stop worrying about losing keys.
For the most part, it had actually worked exactly the way it was supposed to.
One evening, I stepped outside just to grab a package off the porch, still in socks, no phone in my pocket.
I figured I'd be back inside within about fifteen seconds at most.
The door clicked shut behind me.
A second later, the app apparently decided that exact moment was the perfect time to update itself, and it completely locked me out of both the door and my own account.
I didn't even find that part out until much later, of course.
At that exact moment all I knew was that the handle wasn't turning, my socks were getting colder, and I had absolutely nothing on me to fix it.
I stood there on the porch, package in hand, testing the door handle repeatedly, no matter how many times I jiggled it.
Unsurprisingly, it did not change its mind.
My phone was inside.
My spare key was inside.
My neighbor, the one person who had a backup key, was apparently out of town for the entire week, based on her very unhelpfully empty driveway.
I briefly considered climbing through a side window.
I took one look at how high it was off the ground and decided that particular plan would probably just end with a locked door and a sprained ankle.
I sat on my porch steps for a solid twenty minutes, in socks, slightly cold.

I was scrolling through absolutely nothing on a phone I didn't actually have, occasionally rattling the handle again out of pure habit, just staring at my own front door like it owed me an explanation.
Eventually I called the lock company's support line from a neighbor's phone.
After a genuinely painful amount of identity verification, they remotely reset something, and the door finally, mercifully, clicked back open, a solid forty minutes after this whole thing started.
I walked inside, socks now thoroughly ruined from the porch concrete.
I immediately downloaded a physical spare key box, deciding that convenience apparently comes with a small chance of getting stranded outside your own house wearing nothing but socks.
Now I keep an actual metal key hidden nearby, old-fashioned and completely offline.
Apparently the one thing smarter than a smart lock is a backup plan that doesn't need an app update to function.
My neighbor still teases me about it whenever she sees me checking the hidden key spot, usually asking with a completely straight face whether the smart lock has learned any new tricks lately.
